### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cba12d22181588d89fbd45e3a746d5fd356057ec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `92976c622486c14130b3229e9656175a0a758cad` — the merge of head `2aa2ae0a722b39f8cf61eb220e3a263d0e40ffa1` into base `cba12d22181588d89fbd45e3a746d5fd356057ec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 92976c622486c14130b3229e9656175a0a758cad && git checkout 92976c622486c14130b3229e9656175a0a758cad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cba12d22181588d89fbd45e3a746d5fd356057ec 2aa2ae0a722b39f8cf61eb220e3a263d0e40ffa1 && git checkout -B drift-repro cba12d22181588d89fbd45e3a746d5fd356057ec && git merge --no-ff 2aa2ae0a722b39f8cf61eb220e3a263d0e40ffa1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cba12d22181588d89fbd45e3a746d5fd356057ec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2aa2ae0a722b39f8cf61eb220e3a263d0e40ffa1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-server-origin.ts + packages/spec/src/system/push-server-origin.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/push-device-platform.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/MetadataTypeActions.tsx, packages/spec/src/shared/http.zod.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/notifications.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/device-registry.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/user-device.object.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts, packages/spec/scripts/liveness/check-liveness.mts, packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts, .changeset/29642-push-server-origin.md

Inputs read: card #29642 (body, triage 6591841690, ruling 6593872191, the seat's claims, os-dev-report 6595041258), card #29768, PR #29767 body and file list (11 files, +221 −3), the net diff `origin/main...2aa2ae0a` (no overlap with `main`'s newer commits), and the check-runs on the head. The objectstack-ai/mobile tree is not readable from this session, so the shell's saved-server shape is taken from the card text alone.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `RegisterDeviceRequestSchema.origin`: `z.string().regex(PUSH_SERVER_ORIGIN_PATTERN, { message }).optional()`. **Right.** Optional, no default, no transform, so today's bodies parse byte-identically and the three `Iso_` pins stay satisfiable. The one new refusal, a malformed `origin`, is a located 400 at `POST /api/v1/notifications/devices` (`notifications.ts:214-221`): loud, never silent.
2. `UserDeviceSchema.origin`: same leaf and optionality. **Right.** `toUserDevice` (`device-registry.ts:286-303`) builds no `origin` today, so every row the registry answers still parses.
3. `PushDeliveryDataSchema.origin`: same leaf; schema-level `[PLANNED — not yet served]` kept. **Right**, the same declared-ahead shape as `route` in this file.
4. `PUSH_SERVER_ORIGIN_PATTERN` / `PUSH_SERVER_ORIGIN_MESSAGE` (new internal module): **right as an internal name.** No barrel re-exports it (the only importers are the three schema files), mirroring `push-device-platform.ts`; `api-surface/` is untouched.

Grammar read by hand: `^https?://`, then dotted labels `[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?` or a bracketed `[0-9a-f:.]+`, then optional `:` + 1–5 digits, then end. Refused, rightly: uppercase host, trailing slash, path/query/fragment, userinfo, bare host, scheme-relative, non-http schemes, empty, the opaque `"null"`. Accepted, rightly: DNS names, punycode IDN, `localhost`, IPv4, bracketed IPv6, single-label hosts, explicit non-default ports. Out of line with `window.location.origin` (see ④): `http://my_svc:3000` and `https://example.com.` are refused although a browser can answer them; `:443` on https, `:08080`, `:99999` and `[:::]` are accepted although a browser never answers them.

Refusal shape: one `.regex()`, so one issue at `['origin']`, code `invalid_format`, one shared message, pinned on all three carriers; the three JSON Schemas publish one identical `pattern` with `origin` in no `required` list, so `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` has no reason to move and did not.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29642-push-server-origin.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` line-initial; the PR body agrees.
- Kind measured: authorable-surface rows `api/PushDeliveryData:origin`, `api/RegisterDeviceRequest:origin` (`api.json`) and `system/UserDevice:origin` (`system.json`) ⇒ `added`, not `none`; the seat's latest claim agrees. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 ⇒ spec `minor`. `Check Changeset` success. `(widening)` is the right arm; no BREAKING banner; no other package publishes (`packages/client` `registerDevice(request: RegisterDeviceRequest)` widens with the type).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviations (Metadata-protocol `added` vs the claim's `none`; one early run outside the lock; worktree kept): closed; the claim is amended and the readings were retaken under the lock.
- Server half filed as #29768: its build list matches the tree (`user-device.object.ts` has no `origin` column; `device-registry.ts:183-193` writes none; `toUserDevice` reads none; `notifications.ts:222` already passes `parsed.data`). Nothing unowned.
- Console producer rides #29042. **Carried to #29042:** in a sandboxed iframe or an `about:blank` / `data:` context `window.location.origin` answers `"null"`, which this grammar refuses, and the refusal is a 400 on the whole registration body. The Console must send `origin` only when `window.location.protocol` is `http:` or `https:`.
- `[PLANNED — not yet stored]` on the two device-side members plus the schema-level `[PLANNED — not yet served]`: acceptable under the house convention (`api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts:42-46`, `push-delivery.zod.ts`, `push-config.zod.ts`); `check-liveness.mts:502-507` recognises the marker, none of the three is a liveness-governed type, `Spec property liveness` is success, and the test pins the markers so they cannot drop silently.
- Check-runs at read time: every completed gate-carrying run success; 30 (`Build Core`, `Test Core` ×8, `Type Check · workspace` / `consumer gates` / `UI`, `Test UI` ×16, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`) still running; no failure. Landing waits for them.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/push-server-origin.ts` — holds against ruling B.** Every form a deployment actually loads the Console from parses, so no must-fix. Three should-fix items on the same regex, none blocking:
- **should-fix (narrow):** labels follow DNS-hostname grammar, narrower than a URL's domain: `http://my_svc:3000` (a docker-compose service name in a LAN dev setup) and a trailing-dot FQDN are refused although `window.location.origin` can answer them, failing the whole registration with a 400. Allow `_` in a label, or name the limit in the docblock.
- **should-fix (widen):** `(?::[0-9]{1,5})?` accepts non-canonical ports (`:443` on https, `:80` on http, leading zeros, out of range) and `\[[0-9a-f:.]+\]` accepts `[:::]`; a hand-sent `https://crm.example.com:443` would be stored and never match byte for byte. Harmless while the Console is the one producer; tighten or note it.
- **should-fix (prose):** the docblock says "a DNS name or a bracketed IPv6 address"; IPv4 is accepted too (and tested), so say so.

**`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` — holds.** `POST /devices` already `safeParse`s with this schema, so the accept set is what the route enforces from this release. Name precedent verified: `ui/action.zod.ts:1210` names `ctx.origin` "(window.origin)", filled with `window.location.origin` in `MetadataTypeActions.tsx:191`; CORS spells `origins` (`shared/http.zod.ts:122`); `serverOrigin` has zero hits.

**`packages/spec/src/system/push-device.zod.ts` — holds.** The member sits with the registration-mirrored optionals and reads `[PLANNED — not yet stored]`; the registry is honest with it today by omitting it.

**`packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts` — holds.** For objectstack-ai/mobile#174: the shell must compare this value with each saved server's origin (`new URL(saved).origin`), not the saved URL text, which the docblock ("the saved server whose origin it equals") already says. Two saved servers on one origin that differ only by path are indistinguishable by this member; that is the limit ruling B accepted.

No must-fix. The three should-fix items are carried to #29768, which edits this module when the markers come off.
